Remark LR-fusion rigidity: setup, mechanism, examples, and predictions. This remark records the setup, mechanism, worked cases, higher-magic predictions, and proof outlook for Conjecture (diagrammatic double-magic): LR-fusion rigidity at Z, N \in \mathfrak{M}.

A nuclide is double-magic when its proton and neutron counts both fall in \mathfrak{M} = \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\}. Canonical examples include ^4\mathrm{He}, ^{16}\mathrm{O}, ^{40}\mathrm{Ca}, ^{48}\mathrm{Ca}, ^{56}\mathrm{Ni}, ^{132}\mathrm{Sn}, and ^{208}\mathrm{Pb}. The empirical signature is exceptional binding-energy stability: these nuclei occupy sharp local maxima on the binding-per-nucleon curve. The Littlewood-Richardson (LR) fusion of the two saturated Z- and N-blocks is rigid (a single self-conjugate Specht module on the diagonal) and permits no off-diagonal flux.

Setup

Let Z, N \in \mathbb{N} with A = Z + N. The atomic-knot framework (prop:recursive-atom-knot-atlas) constructs the nuclide knot \mathfrak{H}(Z, N) as a fused product of the Z-block (proton braid word at level Z) and the N-block (neutron braid word at level N). On the Hecke side, fusion executes the LR product

  V_\lambda(Z) \otimes V_\mu(N)
  \;\cong\;
  \bigoplus_{\nu \vdash A} c^\nu_{\lambda, \mu} V_\nu(A),

with LR coefficients c^\nu_{\lambda, \mu} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} [ariki1996, ram1991]. The Wedderburn-decomposition support of the categorical mass at level A is determined by the partitions \nu entering the fusion with non-zero coefficients.

The content sum is additive along the LR fusion: c(\nu) = c(\lambda) + c(\mu). The full-twist eigenvalue at level A is q^{c(\lambda) + c(\mu)}. When both \lambda and \mu are self-conjugate (\lambda = \lambda', \mu = \mu', carrying content sum zero), the full-twist eigenvalue at the fused level A is q^0 = 1. The LR fusion is constrained to self-conjugate partitions \nu = \nu'.

Meaning of "rigidity"

The classical LR rule [ariki1996] generally produces a sum over many \nu, with multiplicities counting LR tableaux. The conjecture dictates that at double-magic levels, the sum collapses to a single term with unit multiplicity. Self-conjugacy (\lambda = \lambda', \mu = \mu') constrains the LR product to \nu = \nu'. The saturated-shell content-sum-zero condition (c(\lambda) = c(\mu) = 0) constrains c(\nu) = 0. Rigidity asserts that these two constraints combined leave at most one admissible \nu.

Physically, there is no Wedderburn block at the double-magic level capable of absorbing further binding energy through Hecke channels. Exceptional double-magic stability is the algebraic absence of decomposition channels, not a fitted shell-correction term.

Examples

The illustration blocks Single-magic illustration: ^{18}\mathrm{O} at Z = 8, N = 10, Double-magic illustration: ^{40}\mathrm{Ca} at Z = N = 20 (LR fusion rigid), and Non-magic illustration: ^{6}\mathrm{Li} at Z = N = 3 (frayed both sides) display the diagrammatic content of LR-fusion at the partition level for one representative case from each regime:

  • ^{40}\mathrm{Ca} (Z = N = 20): both blocks are self-conjugate. LR fusion yields a single \nu = \nu' with zero content sum (rigid).
  • ^{18}\mathrm{O} (Z = 8, N = 10): the Z-block is self-conjugate (saturated), but N = 10 \notin \mathfrak{M}. The fusion is non-rigid. The \kappa-leakage from the N side is the algebraic source of the binding tail beyond the saturated Z = 8 contribution.
  • ^{6}\mathrm{Li} (Z = N = 3): neither block is saturated. Frobenius "arms" exceed Frobenius "legs" in both partitions. The fusion produces non-zero full-twist flux vectors, placing the binding curve far from a magic peak.

Predictions for the higher-magic ladder

The combinatorial barrier at k \geq 12 prevents Hoefsmit matrix-evaluation for \{50, 82, 126\}. The LR-rigidity conjecture nonetheless predicts a uniquely determined \nu_{ZN} at each double-magic candidate independent of matrix evaluations. Predicted targets in the higher-magic ladder include ^{132}\mathrm{Sn} (Z = 50, N = 82) and ^{208}\mathrm{Pb} (Z = 82, N = 126). At each target, the LR fusion is conjecturally rigid. The algebraic prediction of the binding-per-nucleon peak is a zero-parameter statement.

The dominant component V_{\lambda_A} in the LR decomposition need not be self-conjugate. Empirical Yamanouchi enumeration finds the dominant \nu is non-self-conjugate at every tested (Z, N). The criterion is content additivity on the LR-fusion, not self-conjugacy of the dominant component.

Discussion

This conjecture is conditional on Categorical neutrality of saturated shells: full-twist identity action on \Phi_n at magic n and Proposition (homological shell condensation): BB-stratified E_\infty^{p,>0}(n) = 0 at magic n. A proof proceeds in two steps: (1) the upstream conjectures force self-conjugate support of \Phi_Z and \Phi_N; (2) a self-conjugacy and content-sum LR rigidity lemma (provable Hecke fragment) collapses the LR product to a single \nu.

Step 2 is plausibly provable in pure Hecke combinatorics. It is not attempted here.

The downstream consequence is the double-magic prediction set. Every binding-energy claim for \{^{132}\mathrm{Sn}, ^{208}\mathrm{Pb}, \ldots\} remains conjectural until the upstream conjectures are closed.

\mathrm{SU}_q(2) rotor bands

The \mathrm{SU}_q(2) rotator model [minkov1996] describes the rotational bands of deformed rare-earth and actinide nuclei. Its Hamiltonian is proportional to the second Casimir of \mathrm{SU}_q(2), with spectrum

where \vartheta is a moment-of-inertia parameter and [\,x\,]_q is a q-number. The deformation is a phase q = e^{i\varphi} with |q| = 1. The q-number [I]_q = \sin(\varphi I)/\sin\varphi yields an oscillatory spectrum. The parameter \varphi is fitted per band. This per-band fit is where the variable moment of inertia enters: \varphi tracks the centrifugal stretching of each rotational band (in the rotator model it is tied to the valence-pair number), so the deformation is a soft, nucleus-dependent softness parameter rather than a single constant. A fixed q_0 therefore does not "absorb" the moment-of-inertia variation — in this model that variation is carried by the per-band fit of \varphi, not by one derived constant, and the claim that a single q captures the stretching is phenomenological curve-fitting, not a fixed-constant derivation.
